item.title: PRECONSTRUCTION ASSOCIATE
item.description:
“CREATING AMAZING SPACES TO BE PROUD OF”

At McCormack, we're one of Australia's leading family-owned building services companies, specialising in fit-out and refurbishment, asset repositioning, design and construct, and heritage restoration.

Our success is built on the strength of our people. We are committed to fostering a workplace where team members are supported to grow, contribute, and do their best work. We value collaboration, integrity, innovation, and creating an environment where everyone feels respected and included.

We have an exciting opportunity for a Preconstruction Associate to join our Preconstruction team in Melbourne.

In this role, you will support all aspects of project design and delivery, including project planning, feasibility assessment, brief development, conceptualisation, detailed design, tender preparation and Design & Construct project delivery. Working closely with our design, estimating, projects and site management teams, you will help drive projects from planning through to design and construction and report directly to the Preconstruction Director.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Coordinate and manage preconstruction activities including project planning, consultant engagement, design development, tender submissions and project handovers.

  • Review tender documentation, assess scope and pricing requirements, prepare reports and presentations, and support successful project bids and client engagement activities.

  • Collaborate with clients, consultants, designers, estimators and project delivery teams to develop design briefs, manage documentation, monitor budgets and programmes, and identify project risks and opportunities.

  • Ensure compliance with relevant building codes, standards and project requirements while supporting seamless handovers and successful project delivery outcomes.

ABOUT YOU

Successful applicants must have:

  • Qualifications in Building & Construction, Project Management, Architecture, Engineering or a related discipline. White Card and First Aid Certificate (or willingness to obtain).

  • Approximately 3-5 years' experience in a Design & Construct, Preconstruction, Design, Project Management or related environment.

  • Prior experience as a Design Manager or Services Manager will be highly regarded.

  • Strong organisational, communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to read and interpret architectural and engineering drawings, manage competing priorities and deliver high-quality outcomes.

  • Experience with project management systems such as Buildlogic, Procore or similar will be highly regarded.

You must have the right to live and work in Australia to be considered for this position. Applications generated or assisted by artificial intelligence (AI) will not be accepted.

WHY JOIN MCCORMACK?

This is an opportunity to be part of a supportive, high-performing and close-knit team that genuinely values its people. We invest in professional development, recognise individual contributions, and create opportunities for our team members to grow their careers.

EMBRACING DIFFERENCES

Being Different Together means creating a workplace where people feel respected, valued and empowered to be themselves. We believe diverse experiences, backgrounds and perspectives make us stronger, leading to better ideas, stronger relationships and greater innovation. We are committed to providing an inclusive environment where everyone has the opportunity to contribute, grow and succeed.

We strongly encourage applications from women interested in construction careers, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, and people with disability. If you require reasonable adjustments during any stage of the recruitment process, please let us know. We are committed to ensuring an accessible and inclusive experience for all candidates.

item.title: SENIOR ESTIMATOR
item.description:
“CREATING AMAZING SPACES TO BE PROUD OF”

We have an exciting opportunity for a Senior Estimator to join our Preconstruction team in Melbourne.

In this role, you will lead the end-to-end estimation process for commercial construction projects, driving successful tender outcomes, managing project risk and commercial viability, mentoring junior estimators, and contributing to the continued growth and success of the business. You will report directly to the Preconstruction Director.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Lead the preparation, review and submission of accurate and competitive estimates, tender responses, take-offs and project budgets for commercial construction projects.

  • Assess project scope, risks and opportunities, engage with subcontractors and suppliers, manage clarifications, and ensure all tender requirements are met.

  • Mentor and support Estimators and Junior Estimators, support with allocating workloads, conduct team briefings, and contribute to the ongoing development of the estimating team.

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with clients, consultants, subcontractors and suppliers while contributing to continuous improvement initiatives and strategic business growth.

ABOUT YOU

Successful applicants must have:

  • A Diploma of Building & Construction or equivalent qualification.

  • More than five years' experience in commercial construction estimation, with demonstrated success managing complex tenders and project pricing.

  • Strong commercial acumen, exceptional attention to detail, leadership capability, stakeholder management skills, and proficiency in construction estimating systems and Microsoft Office applications.

item.title: ASSOCIATE
item.description:
About Us

Studio 103 is an award-winning interior design practice specialising in commercial interiors, with additional experience across retail, government, residential and hospitality. Since 2013, we’ve built a reputation for fresh, sophisticated design that engages and inspires the people who use our spaces.

The Role

We have an exciting opportunity for an Associate to join our Interior Design Team in Brisbane.

As an Associate, you will be a key leader within Studio 103, responsible for driving the successful delivery of projects while leading and developing high-performing design teams. Working closely with the Design Director, you will oversee multiple projects, champion design excellence, foster strong client relationships, and contribute to the strategic growth of the studio.

This role combines design leadership, project oversight, people management, and business development, offering the opportunity to influence both project outcomes and the future direction of the studio.

This role reports directly to the Design Director and plays a critical role in mentoring team members, maintaining quality standards, and supporting Studio 103's continued success.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead and oversee multiple projects from concept through to completion.

  • Drive design quality, project performance and delivery outcomes across project teams.

  • Lead, mentor and develop designers, fostering a collaborative and high-performing culture.

  • Manage client relationships and act as a trusted advisor throughout the project lifecycle.

  • Oversee project resourcing, budgets, programmes and quality assurance processes.

  • Coordinate consultants, stakeholders and project teams to ensure seamless delivery.

  • Contribute to business development, networking opportunities and studio growth initiatives.

  • Support the development of studio processes, standards and continuous improvement initiatives.

About You:

  • Degree qualified in Interior Design or a related discipline.

  • 7+ years' experience in a senior interior design position across commercial, workplace, retail, hospitality and/or residential sectors.

  • Demonstrated experience leading project teams and delivering complex design projects.

  • Strong people leadership skills with a passion for mentoring and developing others.

  • Commercially minded with experience managing project budgets, resources and client expectations.

  • Advanced proficiency in AutoCAD, Adobe Creative Suite and Microsoft Office 365.

  • Exceptional communication, stakeholder management and relationship-building skills.

  • A strategic thinker who is passionate about design excellence, business growth and team success.

You must have the right to live and work in Australia to be considered for this position.

Why work for Studio 103?

We believe exceptional design comes from an inspired and supported team. We offer:

  • Flexible working – practical arrangements that help you balance work and life.

  • Birthday gifting – choose from four curated gift packs sourced from socially responsible suppliers.

  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP) – confidential support for team members and their immediate families.

  • Paid parental & grandparental leave.

  • Professional development – structured reviews and individual development plans, with access to training and internal programs.

  • Diverse project portfolio – a mix of small, large and high end, fast-paced projects that encourage hands-on growth.

  • Service & milestone recognition.

  • Volunteer opportunities – contribute to the community through causes you care about.

  • A fun, supportive and passionate studio culture.

We are proudly an equal opportunity employer. First Nations applicants are encouraged to apply. We recognise that individual differences bring a variety of perspectives, approaches, and talents to the workplace.
